_comment: Tier-2 for sparta hypersonic_flow: a surface heat flux sampled from the first window is not an answer, and the convergence test is agreement between windows rather than the step count. Two decks were run on the installed binary (SPARTA 24 Sep 2025, spa_serial), identical but for the seed: the Mach-5 argon cylinder case, tallied with 'compute surf all all etot' through a 'fix ave/surf' in twelve successive 200-step windows. It exercises the per-surf shapes on the way — compute surf is an ARRAY so it is indexed c_s[1], and a fix ave/surf fed one value is a VECTOR so it is read bare as f_fs. Both runs exit 0 with no error and no warning throughout, which is the point: the run looks entirely healthy while the answer is wrong. THRESHOLD MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, because the flux is a Monte-Carlo tally: the noise floor comes from the late windows of seed A (0.54 percent) and every assertion is then made against seed B, so nothing is tested against a floor derived from itself. Seed B's ten late windows all agree within three times that floor, and both seeds' first window sits more than ten times outside it. CORRECTED: the entry said the first block is 'wrong by a large factor'. It is not — measured, the first window is 1.264 times the converged plateau on both seeds, i.e. 26 percent. That is still tens of times outside the seed spread so it is unambiguously wrong and the advice stands, but an agent told to look for a large factor would see a quarter, decide the transient had passed, and sample it anyway. The entry now gives the magnitude as a percentage and moves the emphasis to the real discriminator: the first window sits outside the seed spread while the late ones agree inside it. No flux value is pinned and no wall-clock is read. COVERS: hypersonic_flow:2. MUTATION CONTROL (added 2026-08-06, re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 prepends a DISCARDED warm-up run of the same length and reads the windows from the second run only (stats_rows keeps the last stats table), so the first measured window already sits in the converged plateau. Seeds, geometry, inflow and window width are untouched; only the transient is removed. Against the measured floor: the first-window excess over the seed-A plateau falls from +0.2642 (seed A) and +0.2644 (seed B) to -0.005991 and +0.002703, against a measured floor of 0.006458 -- the signal lands ON the floor instead of 48x outside it. but_it_is_a_fraction_off_NOT_a_large_factor also goes False because the residual excess turns slightly negative, which is what a converged first window looks like. Verified: unmutated the fixture PASSES (rc=0); with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS (rc=1) and these expect_in_output strings go False and disappear: the_FIRST_window_is_more_than_10x_the_floor=True, but_it_is_a_fraction_off_NOT_a_large_factor=True. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/sparta/surface_flux_needs_steady_state_not_the_first_block && python source.py (passes, rc=0), then T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py (fails, rc=1). Needs a SPARTA binary: the fixtures find spa_serial/spa_mpi on PATH or at ~/Schreibtisch/sparta/src/spa_serial, else set SPARTA_BINARY; with none present they exit 0 on a SKIP: line.
